candidates.title: Modernize Streamlit's default light and dark themes
candidates.section: Modernize Streamlit's default light and dark themes > How?
candidates.text:
### How?

Revisit the default theme tokens and component styling for both light and dark modes, for example:

- **Color palette:** refined neutrals/grays, a more modern primary color, and better semantic colors (success/warning/error/info) with good contrast in both modes.
- **Dark mode:** ensure it's a first-class, well-balanced theme (not just an inversion) — proper surface elevations, borders, and contrast.
- **Typography:** modern default font, refined sizes/weights/line-heights and hierarchy.
- **Spacing & shape:** consistent spacing scale and slightly softer, contemporary border radii and borders.
- **Components:** cohesive styling across widgets, containers, dataframes, charts, etc.

Considerations:
- Accessibility: maintain/improve WCAG contrast in both themes.
- Backwards compatibility: this changes the look of existing apps, so consider how to roll it out (e.g. a new theme version/opt-in, migration notes) to avoid surprising users.
- Keep it fully overridable via the existing `[theme]` config.

candidates.title: Option to set the chart background to something else than the primary background
candidates.text:
### Problem

As of streamlit 1.16 the chart background color has been changed to match the primary color. This can is some cases make graphs difficult to read. Hence I would like an option to set the chart background separately for all pages in a multipage app. 

I have tried to use
```
import plotly.io as pio
pio.templates.default = "none" 
```
I have also tried to add "plot_bgcolor="grey" to the streamlit theme.

But to no avail, the background color stays the same as the primary color.

I can of cause set theme=None in each st.plotly_chart(), but as my app is large this is cumbersome, and will make it difficult to go back to the streamlit theme. 

My suggestion is therefore twofold.
Make a global option for setting the graph theme, either in the config.toml or on the main page.

Add an option to set the graph background color in config.toml like:
`chartBackgroundColer="#F0F2F6" `
or 
`chartBackgroundColer=secondaryBackgroundColor`

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

Best regards Kristian

-----------------------------

Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users.

If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.

candidates.title: st.plotly_chart(,theme = "streamlit") does not use secondaryBackgroundColor as plot background
candidates.text:
### Summary

When updating to streamlit 1.16, our plotly charts change visual appearance due to the new plotly theming. But looking in the documentation it is stated that the secondaryBackgroundColor in the overall streamlit theme (same color as the sidebar) will be used as background color. This is not the case as the background is the same as the backgroundColor, and this makes the plots difficult to read.

It would be nice if the setting was honored or a separate setting was available.

Also it would be nice to have a global setting for the plotly_chart theme selection, instead of per plot. It can be quite time consuming to update this on all pages in a multipage app.

candidates.title: theming
candidates.text:
The following options can be configured separately for the main body of your app and the sidebar. They can also be specified separately for
dark and light themes (`[theme.light]`, `[theme.light.sidebar]`, `[theme.dark]`, `[theme.dark.sidebar]`):

- **Font family**: Set the font family for body text, headings, and code.
- **Font style**: Set the weight and size of heading and code font, and set visibility of link underlines.
- **Text color**: Set the color of body, inline code, and link text.
- **Primary color**: Set the color of interactive elements and highlights.
- **Background color**: Set the color of app, widget, code block, and dataframe header backgrounds.
- **Border radius**: Set the roundness of elements and widgets.
- **Border color**: Set the color and visibility of element, widget, sidebar, and dataframe borders.
- **Basic color palette**: Set the color palette (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet, and gray/grey) for things like colored Markdown text and sparklines.
- **Chart color**: Set series colors for Plotly, Altair, and Vega-Lite charts. Unset light, dark, and sidebar sections inherit from `[theme]`.

### Problem

As of streamlit 1.16 the chart background color has been changed to match the primary color. This can is some cases make graphs difficult to read. Hence I would like an option to set the chart background separately for all pages in a multipage app. 

I have tried to use
```
import plotly.io as pio
pio.templates.default = "none" 
```
I have also tried to add "plot_bgcolor="grey" to the streamlit theme.

But to no avail, the background color stays the same as the primary color.

I can of cause set theme=None in each st.plotly_chart(), but as my app is large this is cumbersome, and will make it difficult to go back to the streamlit theme. 

My suggestion is therefore twofold.
Make a global option for setting the graph theme, either in the config.toml or on the main page.

Add an option to set the graph background color in config.toml like:
`chartBackgroundColer="#F0F2F6" `
or 
`chartBackgroundColer=secondaryBackgroundColor`

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

Best regards Kristian

candidates.text:
### Summary

When updating to streamlit 1.16, our plotly charts change visual appearance due to the new plotly theming. But looking in the documentation it is stated that the secondaryBackgroundColor in the overall streamlit theme (same color as the sidebar) will be used as background color. This is not the case as the background is the same as the backgroundColor, and this makes the plots difficult to read.

It would be nice if the setting was honored or a separate setting was available.

Also it would be nice to have a global setting for the plotly_chart theme selection, instead of per plot. It can be quite time consuming to update this on all pages in a multipage app.
